newsitem.title: USA: Cool, wet weather may aid damaged Plains wheat.
newsitem.headline: Cool, wet weather may aid damaged Plains wheat.

text.p: Forecasts for rain and cool weather in the central and southern Plains could help the hard red winter wheat crop partially recover from last week's spring freeze, meteorologists said.
"If the crop can recover from the freeze damage, then we have the forecast that can do it," said Craig Solberg, staff meteorologist with Freese-Notis Weather.

Forecasts call for rain beginning early Thursday and continuing through Sunday, with four-day totals of one to two inches, with the heaviest amounts likely in the Texas Panhandle and north Texas near Dallas-Ft. Worth.
Freezing temperatures blanketed much of the hard red winter wheat area a week and a half ago, from southern Kansas to the Texas Panhandle, damaging leaves, stems and heads of the crop.
Last week Curtis Thompson, a Kansas State University extension agronomist, said cool, wet weather would allow some of the damaged wheat to at least partially recover.

Joel Burgio, Weather Services Corp meteorologist, forecasted below-normal temperatures late this week for the Plains, with daytime highs in the mid-50s degrees Fahrenheit and lows in the low 30s to mid-40s.
Northern Kansas wheat areas will likely by missed by the late-week rains.
"Most of the Kansas wheat crop could use rain, but the area that needs it the most won't get it and that's northern Kansas," said Burgio.
The spring wheat areas of the Dakotas and Minnesota should remain dry and cool through late this week, with a few light showers likely Thursday in Montana, the meteorologists said.
